subject: ela
intro: The main idea is the most important point a piece of writing makes. It is bigger than any single fact. The smaller facts are the key details, and their job is to support, or back up, the main idea. To find the main idea, ask, "What is this mostly about, and what does the author most want me to understand?" A summary is a short retelling that gives the main idea and only the most important details, in your own words. Leave out the tiny extras.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The tongue does more than one job. It helps you taste sweet and sour foods. It moves food around so your teeth can chew it. It also presses against your teeth to help you make sounds when you speak.

What is the main idea of this passage?

steps: I ask what the paragraph is mostly about.
Every sentence names a job the tongue does: tasting, moving food, and helping you speak.
The point that ties them together is that the tongue does many jobs.
solution.answer: The main idea is that the tongue does many important jobs, such as tasting food, helping you chew, and helping you speak.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Recycling helps the Earth in several ways. It saves trees because old paper can be made into new paper. It keeps trash out of crowded landfills. It also saves energy, since making new cans from old ones uses less power than starting from scratch.

What is the main idea, and which detail supports it?

steps: The first sentence states the big point: recycling helps the Earth in several ways.
The other sentences each give one way it helps.
I choose one of those ways as a supporting detail.
solution.answer: The main idea is that recycling helps the Earth in several ways. One detail that supports it is that recycling "saves trees because old paper can be made into new paper."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Dolphins are very smart animals. They call to each other with clicks and whistles, and each dolphin even has its own special sound, like a name. They work as a team to circle a school of fish so it is easier to catch. Some dolphins have learned to use a sponge to protect their nose while digging for food.

Write a short summary of this passage.

steps: First I name the main idea: dolphins are very smart.
Then I pick the most important examples that prove it: they communicate, hunt as a team, and use tools.
I put these together in a few sentences of my own words.
solution.answer: Dolphins are very smart animals. They talk to each other with special sounds, work as a team to catch fish, and can even use sponges as tools while searching for food.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The first sentence of a news story is very important. Because many readers only glance at the start, the writer packs the biggest facts into it. A good first sentence tells who, what, when, and where all at once. If a reader stops after one line, they still learn the main news.

What is the main idea? Explain how a key detail supports it.

steps: I find the big point: the first sentence of a news story is very important.
I look for a detail that explains why it matters.
The text says a good first sentence "tells who, what, when, and where all at once," which shows why it carries the main news.
solution.answer: The main idea is that the first sentence of a news story is the most important part. This is supported by the detail that a good first sentence "tells who, what, when, and where all at once," so a reader learns the main news even from one line.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Trees are helpful in many ways. Their roots hold the soil in place so it does not wash away in the rain. Their leaves clean the air we breathe. Their branches give shade and homes to birds and squirrels.

What is the main idea of this passage?

steps: I ask what the paragraph is mostly about.
Each sentence gives a way trees help, through their roots, leaves, and branches.
The point that connects them is that trees help in many ways.
solution.answer: The main idea is that trees are helpful in many ways, such as holding soil, cleaning the air, and giving shade and homes to animals.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Amelia Earhart was a brave pilot who broke many records. She was the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic Ocean. She set speed records that no other woman had reached. She also wrote books to encourage other girls to fly.

Name one key detail that supports the main idea that Amelia Earhart broke many records.

steps: The main idea is that she broke many records.
I look for a detail that proves this.
One example is that she was "the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic Ocean."
solution.answer: One supporting detail is that Amelia Earhart was "the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic Ocean." This shows she broke many records.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Ants are tiny, but they are surprisingly strong. A single ant can lift an object many times heavier than its own body. Working together, a group of ants can carry a leaf or even a small dead insect back to their nest. Some ants build long trails and bridges out of their own bodies.

Write a short summary of this passage.

steps: I name the main idea: ants are tiny but very strong.
I pick the most important supporting examples.
I retell it briefly in my own words.
solution.answer: Even though ants are tiny, they are very strong. One ant can lift things much heavier than itself, and by working together, ants can carry large objects and even build bridges with their bodies.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Washing your hands keeps you healthy. Tiny germs live on things you touch, like doorknobs and money. If you rub your eyes or eat with dirty hands, those germs can get inside you and make you sick. Washing with soap and water rinses the germs away before they can harm you.

What is the main idea, and how does a key detail support it?

steps: The big point is stated first: washing your hands keeps you healthy.
I look for a detail that explains why.
The text says washing "rinses the germs away before they can harm you," which supports the main idea.
solution.answer: The main idea is that washing your hands keeps you healthy. A key detail that supports it is that washing with soap and water "rinses the germs away before they can harm you."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The Sun is important to life on Earth. Its light lets plants make their own food, and animals eat those plants. The Sun's warmth keeps our planet from freezing. Even the wind and rain are caused by the Sun heating the air and water.

What is the main idea? Give two key details that support it.

steps: I find the main idea: the Sun is important to life on Earth.
I look for details that show why it matters.
Two supporting details are that its light helps plants make food and its warmth keeps Earth from freezing.
solution.answer: The main idea is that the Sun is important to life on Earth. Two supporting details are that its light "lets plants make their own food" and its "warmth keeps our planet from freezing."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A long time ago, people had no clocks. They told time by watching the Sun move across the sky. Later, they built sundials that used a shadow to show the hour. Then came clocks with gears, and much later, clocks that run on batteries. Today, most people check the time on a phone.

Write a one-sentence main idea and then a short summary of the passage.

steps: First I state the main idea in one sentence.
Then I retell the most important steps in order.
I keep the summary short and in my own words.
solution.answer: Main idea: Over time, the way people tell time has changed and improved. Summary: Long ago people used the Sun and then sundials to tell time. Later they made clocks with gears, then battery clocks, and today most people just use a phone.
